validity.recommendation: Reclassify or de-scope: this is offshore field-development infrastructure (subsea trunk + in-field flowlines linking 7 wellhead + 3 tie-in platforms to the GOSP-4 gas-oil separation complex), carrying multiphase produced fluids from a predominantly OIL increment (475,000 bpd oil vs 750 MMscfd associated gas). It is not a gas transmission trunk, and Fuel=Gas / PipelineType=transmission mis-state what the line is.
validity.researcher_notes: The Marjan Increment is unquestionably real (Aramco's ~$21bn crude increment; McDermott+COOEC won the $1.5bn Package 4 offshore-gas-facilities EPCI in July 2019; GOSP-4 platform delivered from China Aug 2024). But the ROW's classification is the problem. GOSP-4 = Gas-Oil Separation Plant #4, designed to handle up to 475,000 bpd of oil AND 750 MMscfd of gas (offshore-technology, nsenergybusiness). Package 4 scope = three tie-in platforms, seven wellhead platforms, and 540 km of 'subsea trunk lines and in-field pipelines' plus ~90 km of subsea cables. These are offshore GATHERING / production flowlines connecting wellhead platforms to the GOSP and on to the Tanajib onshore complex, not a dedicated gas transmission pipeline. ecns.cn describes the delivered platform as an 'oil and gas collection and transportation system... for collecting and transporting offshore oil and gas to land' i.e. multiphase production, not sales-gas transmission. Labeling this 'Gas Pipeline', Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission is a category error; if GEM keeps it, it should at minimum be flagged as offshore field gathering. The sheet's own McDermott source (mcdermott.com) is 403-blocked and the offshore-energy.biz source is intermittently 502 — the two live-verifiable independent sources both frame this as oil-field development infrastructure.

validity.recommendation: De-dup / reconcile capacity vs P7544. P7545 'Subsea Pipelines' (99.78 km) is a sub-component of the same P7544 'Marjan GOSP-4 Gas Pipeline' network (531 km ~= the 540 km Package-4 subsea trunk + in-field total). Both rows carry Capacity=750 MMcf/d, so the single GOSP-4 gas throughput is double-counted across parent + segment.
validity.researcher_notes: P7544 (len 531.08 km, cap 750) and P7545 (len 99.78 km, cap 750) are the same Marjan GOSP-4 Package-4 subsea system split into network + 'Subsea Pipelines' segment. The 531 km parent matches the sourced 'in excess of 540 km of subsea trunk lines and in-field pipelines'. Assigning the full 750 MMscfd GOSP gas capacity to BOTH rows double-counts it. Recommend capacity live only on the network row (or split), not repeated on the segment. No separate GulfPub feature matches (nearest GulfPub SA-gas records are Fadhili/MGS lines, not Marjan offshore) — so this is an internal GEM parent/segment overlap, not an external duplicate.

validity.recommendation: Verify or footnote the 62 mi / 99.78 km length. No independent source states a 99.78 km subsea line; sourceable Package-4 figures are 540 km total (trunk + in-field pipelines) and ~90 km of subsea CABLES. The 99.78 km appears unsupported and may conflate cables with pipe.
validity.researcher_notes: Length: 62 mi = 99.78 km is cited only to the 403-blocked mcdermott.com page; I could not corroborate it against any live source. The only near figure is '~90 km of subsea cables' (not pipe). Independent sources give the aggregate 540 km subsea trunk+in-field figure (which sits on P7544), not a 99.78 km subsea segment. Capacity 750 MMcf/d IS corroborated but as the GOSP-4 gas HANDLING capacity (offshore-technology, nsenergybusiness), not a measured single-pipeline flow. ConstructionYear=2019 is really the contract-award year (Jul 2019); StartYear=2024 aligns with the Aug-2024 GOSP-4 platform delivery. Owner Aramco 100% and FuelSource 'Marjan oil and gas field' are correct. Endpoints ('Arabian Gulf -> Eastern Coast') are vague but directionally right (offshore Marjan field -> Tanajib onshore complex).

fills.researcher_notes: Marjan field and the entire Increment/GOSP-4 development are wholly owned and operated by Saudi Aramco; McDermott/COOEC are EPCI contractors, not owners. Two independent project sources confirm Aramco as developer/operator. Fills the blank Owner [ref] on the operators/owners tab (oo_sheet_row 5914).

Confirms offshore Marjan field (Arabian Gulf, Eastern Province) to Tanajib onshore complex on the Saudi Eastern coast. Source names the Marjan offshore field, GOSP-4 and the Tanajib onshore expansion. Endpoint labels remain coarse; see routes for named endpoints.

routes.end_name: Tanajib onshore processing complex, Eastern Province
routes.corridor_desc: Offshore-to-shore corridor across the northern Saudi sector of the Arabian (Persian) Gulf: from the Marjan offshore field / GOSP-4 complex (northern Gulf, offshore NE of Tanajib; GOSP-4 sited within ~10 km of GOSP-2/3) south-west to landfall at the Tanajib onshore processing complex on the Eastern Province coast. This is not a single mappable trunk but a web of subsea trunk + in-field flowlines among 7 wellhead and 3 tie-in platforms feeding the GOSP; only the field->shore corridor can be bounded. Endpoints are named and defensible; the exact platform-by-platform routing is not publicly surveyed.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from independent project sources: Marjan offshore field / GOSP-4 (Arabian Gulf) and the Tanajib onshore complex expansion. Coordinates are APPROXIMATE, defensible from the named places (Marjan field in the northern Saudi Gulf sector; Tanajib on the Eastern Province coast), NOT surveyed platform/landfall coordinates — treat as corridor anchors only. No coordinates were fabricated; where a precise point is unknown the approximation is flagged. Given the multi-platform in-field mesh, a corridor at best supports 'low' route accuracy.

summary: P7545 Marjan GOSP-4 subsea pipelines: real project but CONCERN on classification (offshore oil+gas field gathering/production flowlines, not a gas transmission trunk; predominantly an oil increment), duplicate/capacity double-count vs parent P7544 (both cap 750), and unsupported 99.78 km length; owner Aramco + capacity 750 (as GOSP gas-handling) corroborated.
